title: Toronto police officer charged with breach of trust in connection to High Park suicide
article: A Toronto Police officer charged by the province's police watchdog with criminal negligence causing death and failing to provide the necessaries of life in connection with the suicide of a man in High Park earlier this year is facing a third charge.

Tony Loparco, director of the Special Investigations Unit (SIU), announced today that Const. Kyle Upjohn, 33, has been charged with breach of trust by a public officer, which is contrary to Section 122 of the Criminal Code of Canada. The SIU is not elaborating any further on this new charge as the matter is still before the courts.

Daniel Lee, a representative for Upjohn's lawyer, appeared before the Ontario Court of Justice at the Old City Hall courthouse to answer to the three charges earlier today. Lee declined to comment on the case.

Back in June, the SIU said its investigation determined that around 2 p.m. on Feb. 2, 2016, a man sought the assistance of a police officer regarding a suicide attempt by a 19-year-old man in High Park, who according to court documents has been identified as Alexandre Boucher. The young man was pronounced dead at approximately 3:30 p.m. that afternoon. The deceased's family is not speaking publicly about his death.
The SIU is an arm's length agency that investigates reports involving police where there has been death, serious injury or allegations of sexual assault.
